moments.title: An incident: shed the low priority

camera.reason: The frame locked after the zoom-out; stillness lets the two flows be compared
camera.subject: the wide system, the shedder at the intake

objects.change: Before: calm wide system, gauge in calm, tag reads day-to-day. Action: one service inside the API slows (its pulse lengthens), the gauge climbs into strain, the tag flips to incident, and the shedder valve starts dropping hollow requests out of the flow at the intake while solid ones pass. After: critical requests complete; the gauge eases back from its peak; the dropped requests lie below the intake, the rest of the system still standing.

moments.purpose: The viewer needs to see when the shedder acts and what it does: in an incident, it drops low-priority requests so critical ones still get through

recipes.purpose: The system gauge fills from calm into strain and eases back — a qualitative progress fill with no numbers

At the valve, a hollow low-priority request is diverted off the intake path and falls out of the flow to rest below it, while the solid critical request behind it passes. No catalogued rule covers a priority-sorted divert; construction builds it as an alternate motion-path leg on the same request driver

content.question: What separates a rate limiter from a load shedder?
content.takeaway: A rate limiter reads one user's pace and works day to day; a load shedder reads the state of the whole system and acts during incidents, dropping low-priority work so critical work gets through.

continuity.exit: Wide, locked view of the whole system: four user lanes, one rate limiter collar on the focal lane, one load shedder valve on the API intake wired to the gauge (back near calm), requests showing priority but no user tint, and the two families labelled. Scene 4 can split the collar into the request rate and concurrent requests limiters and the valve into the fleet usage and worker utilization load shedders without re-establishing the world.
continuity.entry: Receives the shared API and its users from scene 2, whose fourth situation (an internal failure) already hinted at the system-wide view. This scene opens tight on one user's lane into the API; the context tag already reads day-to-day.

content.development: One continuous world, opened tight and ended wide. We start close on a single user's lane into the API, where a rate limiter sits on that lane and reads nothing but that user's own pace: a burst faster than the pace is partly refused, then the same requests re-sent at an even pace all pass with the same results — the outcome did not depend on the timing. Then the frame makes its single move: one decelerating zoom-out from that one lane to the whole system, where the viewer discovers a second control sitting on the API itself, reading a system-wide gauge. As the camera widens, the requests lose the user tint that told us who sent them and keep only their priority mark, because the load shedder does not ask who. A service slows, the gauge strains, the day-to-day tag turns to incident, and the shedder drops the hollow low-priority requests while the solid critical ones keep flowing. The frame locks wide and the two controls are named side by side by what they read and when they act — the two-family grammar scene 4 fills with four limiters.

demonstration.text: Four user lanes feed one shared API. Close on one lane: that user fires a tight burst of six requests against a rate limiter that reads only their pace; the requests over pace are refused and return to the sender. The same six, re-sent evenly spaced, all pass and produce the same six results. Zoom out to the whole system: a load shedder at the API's intake reads a system-state gauge. A service slows, the gauge moves into strain, and mixed traffic from every lane arrives; hollow low-priority requests are dropped at the intake while solid critical requests continue and complete.
